subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should Windows exec support PowerShell expansion-bearing inline commands through one-shot explicit approval, document them as unsupported, or add a separate script/raw mode?
rationale: Current main intentionally rejects expansion tokens in the approval-analysis path, while the user-visible docs describe a shell command without documenting stripping; changing this affects both Windows usability and command-approval safety.

options.title: Require one-shot approval proof
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and require https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100322 to show redacted live Windows/Gateway proof before merge.

options.title: Document unsupported inline expansion
options.body: Keep the runtime rejection behavior and update docs/tool guidance to steer users to direct commands or `.ps1` script files for expansion-heavy PowerShell.

options.title: Design script/raw mode
options.body: Treat the report as a broader feature request for a separate PowerShell script/raw execution mode rather than changing the existing command approval path now.

recommendation.title: Require one-shot approval proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and require https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100322 to show redacted live Windows/Gateway proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current unresolved behavior is rooted in the Tree-sitter-backed exec authorization planner introduced by this owner path.
